There’s research indicating that almost half of working-age disabled individuals experience chronic loneliness in Britain, which the ONS calls the loneliness capital of Europe. This emphasizes an epidemic of stark isolation, particularly affecting the young disabled population.

A disabled millennial reflects on how even basic social activities feel precarious, highlighting new Scope research showing nearly half of working-age disabled people in Britain are chronically lonely—around 3 million individuals. While the ONS already labels Britain the “loneliness capital of Europe,” with particularly strong effects on young people, the data point to an acute epidemic among disabled people marked by stark social isolation rather than mere feelings of loneliness. ***
